comment: One day of punches per case, read by BOTH test suites so the Telegram
same pairing rule and cannot drift apart silently.
ts_segments / ts_total_minutes are what deriveSegments produces
retrospectively over the whole day (segment entries are [startIndex,
endIndex] into `punches`). py_verbs is receipt.announce()'s verb at EVERY
prefix of the day -- the mid-stream view; '' is the neutral no-claim
receipt. py_so_far_minutes is the hours figure at the day's last punch,
null whenever the receipt must stay silent. Where the two columns
disagree, the disagreement is deliberate and the case comment says why.

cases.name: clean_two_punch_day
cases.case_comment: The ordinary day. Both sides agree completely.

cases.name: lunch_day_four_punches
cases.case_comment: Out and back for lunch at one campus. Both sides agree.

cases.name: double_tap_then_normal_day
cases.case_comment: A second tap three seconds after the first. The retrospective rule pairs the tap (a zero-minute segment) and then reads the lunch gap as a worked hour; the receipt drops the tap as a duplicate, keeps every later verb right, and withholds the hours figure entirely because the two surfaces would disagree on it.

cases.name: clean_rotation_across_two_campuses
cases.case_comment: Morning at one campus, afternoon at another, every punch paired. The afternoon opener's own verb is not claimable mid-stream (arriving at B looks identical to leaving through B's exit device), but it still opens the pair, so the day ends with a full hours figure both sides agree on.

cases.name: departure_through_another_campus
cases.case_comment: The bug that started all of this: a full day at A, then one punch at B on the way out. Whole-day parity called it an arrival. The timeline leaves it unpaired; the receipt says nothing rather than guessing.

cases.name: single_punch_day
cases.case_comment: One punch is an arrival with near-certainty for this roster, so the receipt says so -- the one place mid-stream speaks where retrospection would leave it unpaired. (An out-of-order backlog can make this wrong; nothing at compose time can see a punch that has not been delivered.)

cases.name: lone_labelled_out_is_believed
cases.case_comment: A label beats position on both sides. A lone OUT pairs with nothing, so no hours.

cases.name: repeated_labelled_arrival_keeps_the_first
cases.case_comment: Two labelled INs with nothing between: the first arrival stays open, the repeat is noise, and nothing ever pairs.

cases.name: branchless_punch_breaks_the_run
cases.case_comment: A punch with no mapped branch is its own run on both sides: nothing pairs across it, so the day after it can claim neither a direction nor an hours figure.

cases.name: same_second_double_tap
cases.case_comment: Two rows in the same second. The retrospective rule pairs them into a zero-minute segment; the receipt drops the second as a duplicate and withholds hours.
